- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline after peak at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model may overestimate continuation — reduce forecast slope slightly.
- Model underestimates downward moves when sentiment is negative and recent price is high — add 2–5% buffer to downside forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day average, model tends to overreact — adjust forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term volatility — smooth forecast curve with exponential decay factor of 0.85.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
